content:
alex.king: heads-up — starting a small spike on the console analytics backfill for route_quota -> quota_profile. want to capture tricky atomicity cases.

maria_chen: thanks. what are the invariants we need to preserve?

alex.king: two big ones: 1) any read path during backfill must never return a quota that allows more tokens than pre-backfill intent (no overshoot). 2) analytics rollups (per-route p99) must be consistent for dashboards — temporary gaps ok but no negative counters.

devon: question: are we doing dual-write + shadow read or a migration table + cutover?

alex.king: plan is dual-write to quota_profile (new) and route_quota (old) for 72h, with a readadapter that prefers quota_profile when present. fallback to route_quota if missing.

samir: major failure mode I worry about: partial backfill where a route gets new profile written but not the corresponding rollup tombstones. dashboards might double-count.

maria_chen: agree. we should add a backfill consistency check that computes checksum of bucketed counters for a sample tenant before and after.

ryan: +1 on checksum. also suggest using transactionally consistent update per-tenant via partitioned job — single-threaded per-tenant to avoid races.

alex.king: note: some customers have route re-routing in place — the keying differs (route_id vs route_group). backfill should write both key namespaces.

devon: can we show the key transformation here?

alex.king: code snippet:
```
-- write both keys
INSERT INTO quota_profile (route_key, tenant_id, profile) VALUES (route_id, t, p)
ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE SET profile = EXCLUDED.profile;
-- also write legacy route_quota_index (for readadapter fallback)
INSERT INTO route_quota_index (route_group_key, tenant_id, ref) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
```

samir: what about read performance on console queries? adding quota_profile join might explode 95th percentile queries.

maria_chen: we'll add a readadapter that resolves in-memory mapping: fetch small set of active route keys for tenant and then fetch profiles in a batched call. should avoid wide joins.

ingest-bot: INFO: sample backfill job for tenant t-987 queued (job id: jf-1429).

ingest-bot: WARN: detected 3 routes with mismatched route_group_key in tenant t-987 — skipping until manual review.

ryan: for skipped routes we should emit telemetry + a dashboard row with count, sample route ids, and link to manual remediation runbook.

alex.king: agreed. also adding a safety gate: if more than 0.5% routes skipped in a tenant, pause the tenant backfill and alert #incidents.

devon: how do we test the no-overshoot invariant? simulate concurrent tokens increment while backfill runs?

maria_chen: yes: test harness should run a load generator that hits quota-check endpoints while backfill writes happen. assert token usage reported by readadapter never exceeds baseline by more than epsilon.

samir: suggest small canary: pick 5 low-risk tenants, run dual-write + readadapter there for 24h, run full checks, then open to 50 tenants, etc.

alex.king: rollout plan: canary -> incremental tenant cohorts -> global flip. each step requires green on alignment-check job and <0.1% skipped routes.

ryan: monitoring TODOs: create a console card showing backfill progress (per-tenant %), skipped routes rate, checksum drift, read-latency impact.

maria_chen: do we need a DB migration? schema change is adding quota_profile table + small index. backfill job will populate. plan to deploy schema and backfill in separate deploys?

alex.king: yes deploy schema first (maintenance window for on-prem?), then deploy dual-write code, then start backfill jobs.

devon: for on-prem customers we should provide an opt-in script; can't run large parallel jobs by default.

samir: edge-case: rollback. if we detect drift after flip, what's our rollback plan?

alex.king: rollback is to revert readadapter to legacy read-only route_quota and keep quota_profile writes but stop using them; we'll also run corrective backfills. not ideal but safe.

maria_chen: can we add a preflight that runs a dry-run backfill on a snapshot and reports estimated time + expected skipped count? useful for planning.

alex.king: yep — backing that into the backfill controller.

devon: ok I can pick up the readadapter + canary orchestration. samir you want to own the checksum harness?

samir: I can. will PR the harness and a small dashboard prototype.

ryan: I'll wire the alerting rules and the card in console.

alex.king: thanks all. filing an RFC shortly and will post the canary tenant list. :rocket:

maria_chen: noted. thanks team.
